why: Both appear together in celebration/crediting items and the boundary between celebrating the finished work and crediting makers is easy to blur.

why.T3-009: The item is dominated by completion, pride and 'we did it' celebration of the finished canvas mark.
why.T3-043: It also has distinct thanks and credit negotiation to makers, which T3-009's celebration gate does not cover.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-009 covers celebrating the finished work but not the distinct act of thanking and negotiating credit for makers.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0088523, C0054904, C0023058 and C0174821 are explicit thanks, credit disclaimers, credit reassurance and credit attribution.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-043; we would lose the explicit thanks and credit negotiation, but still have the celebration.

why.T3-017: The concepts are ordinary advice, care, ducks, thesis and a dog vet, with no canvas work or April Fools joke as their point.

why.T3-005: Attack reports, calls to defend and reclaim the breached Protectorate lead the material.
why.T3-021: It also carries distinct monitoring, repair and plan-to-keep concepts.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-005 covers fighting off an attacking force but not the distinct watching, monitoring and routine repair of the mark.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0394220, C0987913, C1001121 and C0470902 are about keeping watch, monitoring disappearance, stopping stray pixels and seeking repair aid.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-021; we would lose the ongoing watch and repair thread, but retain the defence against the attack.

why.T3-001: The item is a run of the room's own April Fools fakes, fake headlines, rebrands and political feints, with replies playing along or being caught.

why.T3-031: Members play with canvas figures through jokes, names and comic embellishments, which is the room's in-joke practice rather than a treaty or build.

why.T3-070: The common practice is making the plan visible and repeatable through coordinates, numbered templates and shared patterns, which is T3-070's gate.

why.T3-005: The codes overwhelmingly report attacks on the flag, calls to defend, hold or reclaim it and fight back against OSU/Blue Corner.

why.T3-002: Most concepts call members to come and place, join, help or donate pixels to the flag.
